declarations.name: BanditRL.OnlineLearning.example_2_10
declarations.signature:
theorem example_2_10 (x0 : ℝ) (hx0 : x0 ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    (∑ t ∈ range T, failureCoefficient t * linearFTLPredict failureCoefficient x0 t) -
      (∑ t ∈ range T, failureCoefficient t * (0 : ℝ)) = (T : ℝ) - 1 - x0 / 2 ∧
    (T : ℝ) - 3/2 ≤
      (∑ t ∈ range T, failureCoefficient t * linearFTLPredict failureCoefficient x0 t) -
        (∑ t ∈ range T, failureCoefficient t * (0 : ℝ))

binder_inputs.reason: initial real decision and finite integer horizon
arbitrary source-feasible initial prediction; not fixed to zero
source-implicit positive horizon used by first-round calculation; no parity restriction

assumption_delta_ledger.detail: Exact exceptional coefficient -1/2, arbitrary feasible initial input, comparator zero, exact -1 and -x0/2, lower bound -3/2.
Positive finite horizon T; no empty-horizon version of the source identity.
Zero-based Lean index t corresponds to source round t+1; strict past excludes current coefficient.

The Lean theorem names one explicit FTL selection family indexed by every feasible x0; it does not quantify over an arbitrary supplied sequence satisfying the argmin rule. The source failure stream has strict nonzero past signs; reader mathematical uniqueness is not advertised as a separate Lean uniqueness theorem.

Generic prefix/minimization helpers accept arbitrary real streams. Objective inequality alone allows infeasible x0 at t=0 because both sums are zero. Pair membership with minimizing inequality to identify feasible FTL.
Deterministic pathwise finite sums. No expectation, stochastic independence, optimal-comparator equality or all-algorithm lower bound.
